Constant Objects and Arrays
The keyword const is a little misleading.
It does not define a constant value. It defines a constant reference to a value.
Because of this you can NOT:

items: Change the elements of constant array
Change the properties of constant object

blocks.text: Difference Between var, let and const

The difference between var, let,
and const lies in scoping mechanisms, reassignment rules, and JavaScript
hoisting.
Modern JavaScript standards recommend avoiding var to minimize unintentional bugs.
Learn More:
JavaScript Scope
JavaScript Hoisting
JavaScript var/let/const
Block Scope

Declaring a variable with const is similar to let
when it comes to Block Scope.
The x declared in the block, in this example, is not the same as the x declared outside the block:

blocks.text: You can learn more about block scope in the chapter JavaScript Scope.
Redeclaring

Redeclaring a JavaScript var variable is allowed
anywhere in a program:

var x = 2;     // Allowed

var x = 3;     // Allowed

  x = 4;         // Allowed

blocks.text: Hoisting

Variables defined with var are hoisted to the top
and can be initialized at any time.
Meaning: You can use the variable before it is declared:

carName = "Volvo";

  var carName;
blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text: If you want to learn more about hoisting, study the chapter JavaScript Hoisting.

Variables defined with const are also hoisted to the top,
but not initialized.

Meaning: Using a const variable before it is declared will result in a
ReferenceError:

alert (carName);

const carName = "Volvo";
